title: Constant-gap NP-hardness of densest k-subgraph
decision_reason: Explicit exact-gap source and independent specialist corroboration; current and unrestricted resolution/version searches; full relevant scope comparisons; mathematical duplicate checks; separated A69 self-review; technical validation passed. No unresolved matching claim located.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Finite explicitly encoded simple undirected unweighted graph G=(V,E), n=|V|, integers 2<=k<=n and 1<=ell<=binomial(k,2).
problem_fingerprint.observable: OPT_k(G)=max_{S subset V, |S|=k} |E(G[S])|, the number of induced edges in the best exactly-k-vertex set.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Does an absolute rational constant lambda>1 exist such that distinguishing OPT_k(G)>=ell from OPT_k(G)<ell/lambda is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions?
problem_fingerprint.reduction_convention: Equivalently, seek one deterministic polynomial-time map taking every Boolean 3-CNF formula to (G,k,ell), taking satisfiable formulas to the high case and unsatisfiable formulas to the low case. Graph size must be polynomial in formula length.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: lambda is fixed independently of n,k,ell; k is part of the input; arbitrary graphs; promise gap; no planted or random input model, ETH, Gap-ETH, Small Set Expansion or planted-clique assumption.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Counting induced edges is equivalent to maximizing either standard density normalization when |S|=k is fixed. Exactly k differs from the variable-cardinality at-least-k problem. Strict soundness inequality follows the source's Definition 1.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One canonical constant-gap NP-hardness question. Do not separately count factors, restricted classes, equivalent density normalizations, or the at-least/at-most variants from this investigation.

statement_sources.locator: Section 1 explicit unresolved constant-factor NP-hardness of DkS; section 1.1 Definition 1 gives the exact gap promise.

publication_state: Accepted research draft and evidence uploaded directly to main; exact research commit separately verified September 19, 2026. No permanent ID or active catalogue integration.

nearest_existing_entries.difference: Average-case detection in an independently sampled Erdos-Renyi graph with a planted clique; target is an unconditional worst-case polynomial reduction for an edge-count promise.
Almost-satisfiable permutation constraints with an alphabet fixed by error; target is fixed-cardinality graph selection. No equivalence or consequence from Unique Games alone is asserted.
Exact deadline feasibility on three identical processors. Its evidence mentions a sparse DkS assumption, but the catalogue does not state the present graph-selection question.
Power-of-job-count hardness for precedence schedules on prescribed machines; distinct objective, input model and requested gap.

duplicate_check.current_search: Repository-wide densest-subgraph, constant-gap, densest-k-set, k-cluster, induced-edge and min-union searches found no equivalent active or accepted entry. Discovery-only references and the scheduling hypothesis were inspected.
duplicate_check.family_policy: One canonical fixed-gap question; no extra count for approximation factors, weighted variants, equivalent normalizations, at-most/at-least variants or downstream reductions.
duplicate_check.upstream_refresh: September 19: fetched origin/main and HEAD both 8e0dae5a6e83cac559df71ace366dd0dccb9aeab. Connected GitHub confirmed private MColbrook/AIM, push permission, no open PRs and only main; second branch page was empty.

independent_corroboration.primary: LMT26 section 1 explicitly leaves constant-factor NP-hardness unresolved and Definition 1 supplies the exact gap.
independent_corroboration.independent: JPRX23 section 1.4 and CDGT23 introduction explicitly retain this same gap; their author teams are disjoint from LMT26.
independent_corroboration.not_counted_twice: M17 and LMT26 share Manurangsi. Preprint/conference/journal versions are one work. LMFB24 is model/application/algorithm background, not claimed as an explicit formulation of this exact NP-hardness question.

normalization_checks: One rational lambda>1 works independently of n,k,ell. A weaker rational gap can replace any real gap.
The input has exactly k selected vertices and nonnegative unit edge weights. Density by k or binomial(k,2) has the same approximation ratio at fixed k.
Allowing at most k while maximizing raw nonnegative edge count is equivalent by padding; this does not identify variable-cardinality density objectives.
The strict low-case inequality is that of LMT26 Definition 1. The integer threshold and explicit graph encoding exclude precision or succinct-input ambiguity.
NP-hardness requires a deterministic polynomial-size map from every 3-CNF; ETH, Gap-ETH, planted distributions, or a superpolynomial reduction are insufficient.
A lambda-approximation distinguishes the promise by comparing its returned edge count with ell/lambda. Exact CLIQUE hardness alone leaves only a gap tending to one.
No equivalence to P versus NP, no dichotomy between constant approximation and NP-hardness, and no statement that all constant factors are hard is asserted.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Hardness of DALkS below 3/2 assuming all fixed-factor GapDkS problems hard.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Neither its premise nor its conclusion proves existence of one unconditional NP-hard gap for DkS.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Hardness below 2 for DALkS under stronger PolyGapDkS or Strongish Planted Clique assumptions.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Additional hypotheses and changed objective; no unconditional 3SAT map.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Exact DALkS is W[1]-hard when parameterized by k.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Exact parameterized hardness does not give a constant approximation gap.

resolution_comparisons.locator: Section 1.1, Theorem 1 and following reduction-size discussion
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Under ETH, almost-polynomial ratio hardness even with a clique in the high case.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The reduction regime is not polynomial in the source formula size; conditional exclusion of polynomial algorithms is not NP-hardness under the target reduction convention.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Near-polynomial gap under Gap-ETH, stated for subconstant exponents f(n).
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Retains Gap-ETH and does not construct the required unconditional polynomial-time map.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: O(n^(1/4+epsilon)) approximation in n^O(1/epsilon) time for fixed epsilon; exact exponent 1/4 via quasipolynomial time.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Neither is a constant-factor polynomial-time guarantee; taking epsilon=0 is invalid.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: High-probability pseudoexpectations on random null graphs, k=n^alpha with alpha in (0,1/2], p=n^-beta, q=n^-gamma and gamma>alpha beta; high-degree SoS gaps.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: A lower bound against this relaxation family does not quantify over all algorithms or produce NP-hardness reductions.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Exact hardness of complete weighted beta-metric selection by weights 2 beta on original edges and 1 elsewhere.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The additive baseline binomial(k,2) preserves the exact optimizer, not a new unconditional constant gap.

resolution_comparisons.locator: Section 2, Lemma 1 and Theorems 2-3 with proofs
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Polynomial and parameterized approximation barriers assume Planted Clique and Strongish Planted Clique respectively.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Actual full theorem hypotheses resolve the ambiguous inapproximability wording in the abstract; no matching unconditional claim.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Ordinary DkS is the special case of attribute-constrained DkS with all group minimum counts zero.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Hardness transfers outward to a generalization; it is not a new hardness theorem for the starting problem.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Diagonal loading permits integral global optima; Frank-Wolfe converges to a stationary point of a nonconvex problem.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Tightness and stationarity do not provide polynomial global optimization or a uniform constant approximation.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: ETH-based semimetric diversity hardness via weights 2 sigma and 1.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The reduction imports M17 conditional DkS hardness; it does not remove ETH.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Subpolynomial approximation hardness follows from a d(n)-to-d(n) 2-CSP hardness conjecture.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The conjectural source-gap assertion is not established by the reduction, so this does not solve the target.

resolution_comparisons.locator: Introduction, pp.38:2-38:3, explicit Khot result restatement
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: No PTAS under NP not contained in the intersection, over epsilon>0, of BPTIME(2^(n^epsilon)).
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: This is stronger than P not equal NP. Unqualified no-PTAS background sentences in two 2024 papers cite this result and cannot be upgraded to the requested NP-hardness.
